sessions.title: What’s New in Kotlin: Language and Ecosystem Strategy
sessions.description:
In this talk, I’ll share key updates from the Kotlin ecosystem, with a strong focus on language features and libraries.

We'll cover topics such as Kotlin's error model, the story around value types and immutability, new initiatives in IDE support, and upcoming changes in the runtime.

sessions.title: 47 Refactorings in 45 Minutes
sessions.description:
IntelliJ IDEA's refactoring support is second to none, but the Refactor This menu only has 9 items. Where is all the power hiding?

Join Dmitry and Duncan on a whistle-stop live-coding tour of our favourite IDE's invisible refactorings. Marvel as Alt-Enter reveals refactorings before your very eyes. Gasp as they change depending on context. Wonder how completely different they can be simply by moving the cursor one character to the left or right, and feel the tension mount as they approach the deadline. Can they really show more than one refactoring a minute?

sessions.title: KotlinJS and why I love it
sessions.description:
While everybody dreams about WASM, KotlinJS is more and more overshadowed by it.
This talk will reflect on the good, the bad and the ugly parts which are inherent in KotlinJS.

sessions.title: How to kill JavaScript from your Stack with HTMX and Kotlin
sessions.description:
Modern web development is complex.
Building an interactive full-stack web application often requires TypeScript, a JavaScript framework, third-party libraries to handle routing and data fetching, a JSON API, serialization, and a database.

To reduce this complexity, one alternative is using server-side HTML templating engines like Thymeleaf or Handlebars.
However, this approach sacrifices interactivity and component composability, and it introduces the risk of template breakage whenever the data model changes, due to the lack of static compilation.
Additionally, you still need to learn and understand the templating language syntax.

In this talk, discover how to quickly build a full-stack web application without relying on a templating engine or a frontend framework.
We’ll bypass the complexity of JSON and REST APIs altogether.
Instead, experience the power of Kotlin DSLs, which allow you to write expressive, composable and type-safe code,
and achieve a user experience rivaling Single Page Applications by using HTMX for dynamic interactions without JavaScript.
Using a simple web application as an example, we'll explore how to do routing, page transitions, real time validation, and write components that can be reused across pages.

By the end of this session, you’ll gain a fresh perspective on building modern web applications efficiently and effectively.

sessions.title: Building AI agents in Kotlin with Koog
sessions.description:
AI provides great new opportunities for powerful user interactions, and Kotlin is uniquely positioned to implement them! In this session, we’ll see how you can enhance your applications with AI capabilities, including the ability to create complex agentic workflows. We'll do so by diving into Koog, the multiplatform framework built by JetBrains that designed to build agents in idiomatic Kotlin. We'll see what it takes to get started from scratch, and how Koog covers not just basic cases, but provides you everything you need to scale your AI agents in production deployments.

The talk starts the audience off at zero, and then introduces the core concepts of Koog, such as executors, graphs, and nodes, walks through some actual code examples, and also provides an overview over the advanced features we've built for koog.ai, such as history compression and observability / tracing. Listeners will walk away with a good basic and practical understanding to support their own adventures with Koog in a multiplatform setting.

sessions.title: Simple Parser Combinator in Kotlin
sessions.description:
Building a JSON or any other parser with Parser combinators in kotlin
How a single function can build a complete and simple parser framework, use it to parse our JSON example.

sessions.title: FP and OOP: Best Friends Forever?
sessions.description:
Modern programming languages are increasingly becoming a mix of multiple paradigms. Object-Oriented Programming languages (OOP) like Java and Kotlin, for example, are being further extended with concepts from Functional Programming languages (FP). Think of immutability and lambda expressions. What happens when we combine both programming styles in a single codebase? Can OOP and FP complement each other?

In this talk, we'll explore what happens when we introduce FP patterns in OOP code. Perhaps it will turn out that OOP and FP are indeed BFFs!

sessions.title: Making Spring Boot, OpenAPI, and @Transactional play nice with Arrow's Either
sessions.description:
Arrow’s Either is a very useful tool to propagate business errors, but integrating it with Spring Boot is not straightforward. Spring assumes exceptions for error flow like @Transactional rollback, and OpenAPI-generator expects ExceptionHandler for non-200 responses.

In this talk, we’ll show how we wired Either into a Spring Boot + OpenAPI stack, overcoming ACID pitfalls despite freely mixing @Transactional, TransactionOperations, and Either.

The result: APIs that return functional 400 errors and transaction rollback across multiple transaction layers, without using exceptions.

sessions.title: Can LLMs play text adventures? – Kotlin edition
sessions.description:
The title says it all! In this talk, we will explore the gaming capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). Since the release of ChatGPT, these models have seen steady improvements. Given that the second 'L' in LLM stands for 'Language,' it’s fitting that one of the most obvious games to play with an LLM is a text adventure. By the end of this talk, you’ll discover whether, and how well, LLMs can navigate and play text adventures.

I made a little tool that hooks up LLMs with text adventures. This will be used in the demos. The first version is built in Java, but for this conference I put together a Kotlin version.

sessions.title: Exploring and Analyzing Data as a Kotlin Developer
sessions.description:
What can data science bring to Kotlin developers? How can we make it as easy as possible for Kotlin developers to start handling data using the tools they already know and love?

In this talk, we'll find out how easy it is to get started, explore and modify data received from an API without installing complex frameworks, learning an entirely new language, or even leaving your IDE!

We'll dive into the work of the Kotlin Data Science team at JetBrains. This includes tools like Kotlin Notebook in IntelliJ, the open-source Kotlin DataFrame library (which I'm personally involved in) and its first-of-a-kind compiler plugin, and Kandy, an open-source Kotlin-like plotting DSL.

We'll use Kotlin notebooks as a powerful, flexible, yet familiar programming tool; parse, wrangle, and explore typed data from a simple API using DataFrame, and plot the results with Kandy.

Finally, we'll have a small look at what the experimental DataFrame compiler plugin can do and how it might change the way you program Kotlin code in the future!

sessions.title: Vibe code a Kotlin compiler plugin
sessions.description:
Vibe-driven development is often associated with rapid prototyping, particularly in frontend applications. However, its underlying principles of embracing intuition and iterative progress can be a powerful methodology for navigating highly complex software domains.

In this session, I will demonstrate how I applied this unconventional approach to build a fully functional Kotlin compiler plugin.

sessions.title: Deprecate symbols from your libraries… Why and how?
sessions.description: When you bundle third-party classes into your own module, they often leak into the public API — even though you never intended them to be public. Normally you’d relocate them to a different package, but sometimes constraints prevent this. In this talk, I’ll share how we solved this problem in the Kotlin Gradle plugin by applying bytecode transformations that deprecate bundled library symbols, discouraging their use in downstream code and the story behind. I’ll also show how the same idea can be applied to regular dependencies, giving you more control over which parts of a library are actually available to your project.

sessions.title: Javascript is Dead: the Past, Present, and Future of Full‑stack Development
sessions.description:
Over the span of my career, I've seen Javascript evolve from a simple browser scripting language into the most popular programming language in the world.  While some might love it, I would argue that its popularity is driven almost entirely by its runtime.  With Web Assembly opening the door for other languages, it's time to re-evaluate how we approach coding for the web.

I'll give a brief history lesson on the evolution of the full-stack developer over the last 20 years, then describe my experience working on a huge Kotlin web project at Jetbrains, and finally I'll talk about the many ways we're improving the experience in Ktor.

sessions.title: Supercharge your LLM with Kotlin 💪: Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Action
sessions.description:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is said to become the 'HTTP of AI'. Bold claim or inevitable reality? In this talk, we'll crack open the LLM black box and discover how MCP seamlessly bridges AI with the real world.

Get to know how MCP transforms your language models from impressive chatbots into powerful, connected agents that can tap into APIs, query databases, and execute complex workflows—all through a beautifully simple, pluggable architecture.

We will witness live MCP magic with real-world off-the-shelf integrations that boost any (development) workflow with jaw-dropping automation, making you rethink what's possible. And yes, we will also consider the less exciting aspects of MCP like security and deployment as well as what the future holds to solve these 'issues'.

Finally, get to know how easy it is to build your own MCP server in Kotlin using the official Kotlin SDK, so you can bridge any productivity gap you might encounter yourself.

By the end, you'll understand not just how MCP works, but how to wield it as your AI superpower. With MCP, your AI will never taste the same!

sessions.title: Lessons learned after building apps with Kotlin Multiplatform
sessions.description:
With Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform, you can share code and UI across multiple platforms, from Android and iOS to macOS, Windows, and Linux. But building apps on all these platforms brings unexpected challenges you don’t anticipate at the beginning.

In this talk, I’ll share what I’ve learned (often the hard way) while developing apps with Kotlin Multiplatform. You’ll hear why sharing less code can sometimes save more time, how dealing with the iOS Keychain from background services turned into a debugging odyssey, and why placing your database in the wrong Windows folder can lead to silent data loss during app updates. We’ll also cover sandboxing on macOS, the trade-offs between using interfaces and `expect/actual`, and the complexities of distributing apps across platforms.

Whether you’re just getting started with Kotlin Multiplatform or already deep into it, this talk might just save you from a few future debugging headaches.

sessions.title: Beyond data classes: Kotlin‑powered domain modeling
sessions.description:
Proper domain modeling is one of the key elements in building robust software. Kotlin offers powerful tools for effective modeling, making it an excellent choice for developing backend systems that handle business logic in complex domains.

In this talk, I'll demonstrate how Kotlin's features make it the ideal tool for domain modeling, empowering developers to create models that are clear, readable, meet business requirements, and remain resilient to change. I'll explain how concepts like sealed/inline classes, extension functions, constructor overloading, and several others help enrich models, making them more expressive and less error-prone. During the presentation, I'll refactor real-life code to transform anemic domain structures into something far more idiomatic, legible, and efficient.

sessions.title: Let’s use IntelliJ as a game engine, just because we can
sessions.description:
Ever wondered what would happen if you used IntelliJ IDEA as a game engine? Probably not, but Alexander did, and it turns out, it’s absurd and a lot of fun! Join Alexander for a lighthearted yet insightful dive into the absurdness of using one of the most sophisticated IDEs to create games within your codebase because... well, why not?

In this talk, Alexander will walk you through his adventure of using the IntelliJ plugin platform in combination with Kotlin to implement game logic, render graphics, and more. He’ll share the head-scratching moments, the "aha!" breakthroughs, and the plain stupidity of making this idea work. You'll see IntelliJ handling sprites, game physics, and maybe even a rogue mutable variable trying to destroy your cursor!

This session is for anyone who believes that the best projects are born from a spark of curiosity and a sense of fun. Discover how pushing the boundaries of your tools can lead to unexpected innovations and a lot of laughs along the way. After all, the most important work we do is often the work we find the most fun. Come ready to chuckle, learn, and maybe even be inspired to try your own offbeat experiments!

sessions.title: Snake in 10 Lines of Kotlin: Learning More by Coding Less
sessions.description:
Can you create a complete game with just 10 lines of code? That was the quest I set myself when recreating the classic game Snake in as few lines as possible. Let me tell you: I was not ready for the types of challenges I would face. For example, just registering button presses was not as straightforward as I had hoped.

Through live coding, I will show you how I overcame these obstacles and distilled Snake to its absolute essence. What key elements make this game instantly recognizable? By combining Kotlin and Swing, we will end up with a minimal code base and if not award-winning, at least a playable version of Snake.

Striving for conciseness led me to a deeper understanding of the code. I will show how constraints push us to think outside the box and lead to more creative solutions. Moreover, my approach can be applied to any problem. Sometimes the best way to understand code is by seeing how little of it you actually need!

sessions.title: Build your own NES Emulator... with Kotlin
sessions.description:
Let Fools Dream

For those who have ever wanted to recreate classic games, this presentation covers my five-year journey to build a NES emulator in Kotlin. Starting from scratch in 2020 (you can probably guess why), I’ll share the challenges posed by the architecture of old hardware, performance optimization (surprise, surprise), and the difficulties of emulating sound. I’ll also highlight which Kotlin features shine (and why concurrency isn’t one of them). This high-level overview will walk through each step of the process—from reading ROM formats to where GPT can help, though it won’t write the code for us just yet. We’ll wrap up by launching Mario on the emulator (hopefully without a call from Nintendo).

sessions.title: Building a Modern Kotlin Multiplatform Application with Compose Multiplatform and Koin
sessions.description:
The world of cross-platform development is rapidly evolving, with Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform leading the charge for creating shared codebases that work seamlessly across Android, iOS, and beyond. Let’s dive into building modern and efficient multiplatform applications, with Koin as the go-to framework for effortless dependency injection.

We’ll cover best practices for integrating KMP, organizing shared and platform-specific code effectively, and using Compose Multiplatform to deliver a consistent and engaging Multiplatform UI experience. We’ll point to how the official “Now in Android” demo can be lifted into a KMP/Compose/Koin setup—highlighting key integration steps without rewriting every line of code in the talk itself. Along the way, you’ll learn typical pitfalls (e.g., code-sharing patterns, DI scoping, Compose performance heuristics) and practical guidelines for keeping your code maintainable and performant.

Are you ready to elevate your Kotlin cross-platform development skills?

sessions.title: Bullseye or Backfire? Arrow in Kotlin Without the Poison
sessions.description: Kotlin’s Arrow library can spark strong opinions: some see it as a game-changer, others as unnecessary complexity. But what is Arrow really about, and how can it help us write better Kotlin? In this talk, we’ll look at where Arrow fits in everyday code, why it can lead to clearer and more reliable applications, and how it can be introduced without overwhelming teams. We’ll explore practical examples and share lessons learned from using Arrow in real projects. By the end, you’ll walk away with a balanced perspective on how to use Arrow as a tool to hit your coding goals, without the fear of it turning into something toxic.

sessions.title: Kotlin Meets AI: How Agents Reshaped the Way I Build Projects
sessions.description:
AI and AI agents are reshaping how we think, plan, and create software. In this talk, I share my personal journey as a lead engineer learning to work with these tools — where they fit, how to delegate to them, and what new skills the process revealed.

It's a story of experimentation and gradual workflow change, discovering a way to build not just faster, but more thoughtfully — with more space for clarity and creative thinking.

sessions.title: Kotlin Clean Architecture for Serverless: Business Logic You Can Take Anywhere
sessions.description:
As cloud platforms continue to evolve, serverless functions provide powerful ways to build and scale applications with reduced infrastructure concerns. However, cloud-specific requirements often make it challenging to keep business logic portable across different cloud providers. This session presents a variant of clean architecture designed to separate core business logic from cloud-specific code, leveraging Kotlin’s capabilities along with Spring Cloud Function and headless Gradle modules.

In this talk, I’ll demonstrate how to structure a Kotlin application for serverless using a clean architecture approach for serverless. This structure maintains cloud-agnostic business logic while allowing platform-specific implementations for integration functionality like storage. By isolating business logic in headless modules, developers can deploy the same core code across multiple cloud function providers such as AWS Lambda and Azure Functions.

Through live coding, we’ll explore practical techniques for building and deploying serverless applications with cloud-agnostic business logic. 
This session is aimed at Kotlin developers interested in serverless architecture, cloud flexibility, and clean architecture principles.

sessions.title: Exploring improvements to 'when'
sessions.description:
In this talk we look at improvements related to control flow in Kotlin since version 2.0, and how they influence how the code is written:
- Guards to describe side conditions to matches,
- Context-sensitive resolution to omit redundant qualifiers,
- Better exhaustiveness checker.
On top of the syntactic improvements, the talk also discusses how these features interact with smart casting and null safety.

The goal of the talk is to give the audience a deep understanding of all the possibilities of Kotlin matching by version 2.2/2.3 and beyond. Most of the talk consists of examples and refactorings that improve safety or readability.

If time allows, we may also explore some upcoming developments, like subtyping reconstruction.

sessions.title: Rediscovering Apollo 11: Using Spring AI to Explore the trip to the moon!
sessions.description:
What happens when you combine Apollo program data with modern AI tools? You unlock a whole new way to explore one of humanity’s greatest adventures!

In this session, I’ll show you how to use Spring AI to:

- Enhance search with vector embeddings, making sense of mission transcripts and images.
- Dive into chunking, summarization, and extraction to improve retrieval precision
- Explore how RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) enhances answers by grounding LLM responses in real Apollo data
- See how Semantic Cache reduces cost while speeding up searches.

Don’t know what embeddings, RAG, or vector databases are? No worries—I’ll break it all down and show you how it works.

Come for the Moon missions, stay for the AI magic, and leave ready to build your own intelligent search experiences!

sessions.title: wAIred! Learn with(out) AI
sessions.description:
In today's world, artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the way we learn. This talk will explore how we can use AI tools to enhance our learning experiences. We will try out some AI tools that can help with planning, practicing, researching etc.

But as we embrace these new technologies, we must also ask ourselves: Are we becoming less capable of thinking for ourselves? Do these tools make us smarter, or do they risk dulling our critical thinking skills? This talk will encourage us to think critically about the role of AI in our education. Together, we will discover how to use AI to support our learning journey while still developing our ability to think critically.

sessions.title: Coding at the Speed of Thought: Kotlin, Compose, and the Power of Vim
sessions.description: Want to write Kotlin as fluidly as you think? This talk shows how using Vim inside IntelliJ supercharges your Kotlin development, especially with Jetpack Compose and coroutine-heavy code. You’ll learn how motions, macros, and modal editing can make you dramatically faster at navigating and refactoring Kotlin code. With live coding demos, you’ll see a real-world workflow in action. From building composables to wrangling Flow, all without even lifting your hands off the keyboard.

sessions.title: Roundtable: Kotlin by JetBrains, present and future
sessions.description: Have a chat with Developers & Developer Advocates from JetBrains about anything Kotlin related on your mind. Language evolution, tooling, development practices, Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform... We're here for all of it!

sessions.title: Kotlin multiplatform + Domain models = ❤
sessions.description:
In most applications we write, the core domain model with all its crucial business logic only lives in the backend to ensure consistent behavior of a system. With Kotlin multi-platform, that same domain model can suddenly also be used in your user-facing mobile apps and frontends.

Learn what that means for the applications you build. What does your code look like when you share your domain model? How do you ensure that that domain model is re-usable? What kind of trouble can you run into and what techniques can you use to avoid that trouble? And how does the ability to use the full domain model benefit the user experience? And last but not least, how can your organizational team structure make this way of working a huge success or a road towards disaster?!

sessions.title: Framework-Free, Future-Proof: Isolated DDD in Kotlin with (and without) Spring
sessions.description: If you want to isolate your domain from your plumbing (you want to), said domain is only truly isolated if it is free from your framework. For Spring this means you cannot use its dependency injection. In this talk I will show you how it can be done with just Kotlin and explore the additional benefits of this approach.

sessions.title: Own your design: functional principles vs framework
sessions.description:
Frameworks like Spring often tempt engineers into shortcuts that compromise clean design, such as primitive obsession or exception-driven error handling. In this session, we will explore how to reclaim control by applying Domain-Driven Design, hexagonal architecture, and functional programming principles—illustrated entirely with Kotlin, a language I have been using professionally since 2019.

We will focus on three key principles for a functional approach:
• Avoid primitive obsession by modeling rich domain types
• Apply interface segregation to reduce coupling and keep boundaries clean
• Treat errors as first-class citizens through functional error handling

Attendees will leave with practical strategies to keep domain logic clean and resilient, ensuring design—not the framework—remains at the core of the solution.

sessions.title: KtLint behind the scenes. Why it matters and how to extend it.
sessions.description: The Ktlint ecosystem is robust and highly adaptable, making it easy to integrate into any team's development workflow. By adopting Ktlint in your projects, you ensure a consistent code style and improved readability across your codebase—key factors that directly enhance team productivity and collaboration. And if the default formatting rules don’t fully meet your needs, Ktlint empowers you to define and implement custom rules tailored to your team's conventions. In this session, you'll learn not only why Ktlint is a valuable tool, but also how to extend it to fit your unique coding standards.
